<!-- pr-reviewer: 6637e92c6e868b17ddd437b357b579a9f9afd689 -->
**Ready for the maintainer to merge.**

Independent review of head `6637e92c`. I trial-merged it with current `origin/main` (`7a5816cf`) and the merge was clean. I built it, ran every suite the quick plan maps the diff to, ran clippy, and probed the new rule with my own throwaway tests (not pushed).

### What looks good
- The fix measures what #1205 asks for. A facet is excused only if it reads as a round wall of a hole the op declares. Its sagitta about that hole's axis (nearest vertex radius less nearest approach, `hole_wall.rs:84-106`) must be at most `WALL_SAG` = 0.05 mm. The excuse is `min(sagitta, old chord dip)` (`hole_wall.rs:76`), so the new rule can only convict more than main, never less. My probes confirm this: no case convicts on main and passes here.
- The excuse is bounded by an absolute depth and no longer grows as the tool shrinks. That was the root of the bug.
- It fails closed in every case. No holes named, a hole axis not parallel to the move's tool axis (`probe.rs` `axis_xy`), or a non-finite or zero-length axis or facet each excuse nothing. The new code has no `unwrap`/`expect`/`panic!` outside tests.
- All four kinds go through one function, `wall_excuse`: drill, bore and thread via `generate.rs` `contain_into`, and cross drill via `cross_part.rs` with each cross hole's own line.
- `solid_law_goldens.rs`: only its `contain_law` helper changed, so it now names the holes it drills (with no holes named, the new law would excuse nothing). No `.cl`/`.nc` golden, no assertion and no tolerance moved, and all its goldens stay clean. Nothing was loosened. `bore_facet_sagitta` and `bore_entry` are untouched and green.
- The body states the one fixture whose op verdict now convicts (`tap_sim`, the square hole under an M6 tap) and explains why that conviction is correct. The decision record explains the 0.05 cap and lists the options considered and dropped. The new module carries its provenance line.
- Process: conventional subject, a `Changelog:` line, ends `Fixes #1205`. No `CHANGELOG.md`, snapshot PNG or process files touched.

### Local results (merged with main)
| Step | Result |
|---|---|
| `cargo clippy -p camcraft-sim -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings` | clean |
| camcraft-sim lib + 20 sim suites from the quick plan | 244 passed, 0 failed, 1 ignored |
| camcraft-motion `real_tip`, `solid_law` | 9 passed, 0 failed |
| camcraft-app lib + every app suite in the quick plan (incl. `hole_wall_flats` 4/4, `solid_law_goldens` 5/5, `bore_entry` 3/3, all `drilling_cross*`, `operations` 117) | all green |
| Extra: `tap_sim` 2, `golden_cl` 25, `bore_facet_sagitta` 2, `conformance` 6, `center_cut_multiaxis` 6 | all green |
| camcraft-app total | 741 passed, 0 failed, 11 ignored (lib + 81 binaries) |

### Probe readings
These come from throwaway tests: an 80x80 plate with a blind polygon hole, corners on the stated radius. "Main" is the same tree with the pre-#1205 rule switched back on locally. Each cell is blocking gouges.

| Bore op at r 5, tool diameter | 1 | 2 | 4 | 6 | 8 | 9 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| octagon r5 (PR / main) | 10 / 10 | 10 / 10 | 10 / **0** | 10 / **0** | 10 / **0** | 10 / **0** |
| hexagon r5 | 10 / 10 | 10 / 10 | 10 / 10 | 10 / **0** | 10 / **0** | 12 / **0** |
| square r5 | 10 / 10 | 10 / 10 | 10 / 10 | 10 / 10 | 12 / 10 | 12 / 10 |
| D-bore (96-gon r5, flat at Y 4) | 4 / 4 | 4 / 4 | 4 / 4 | 4 / **0** | 4 / **0** | 12 / **0** |
| 16-gon r5 (sag 0.096, over the cap) | 6 / 6 | 10 / 0 | 10 / 0 | 10 / 0 | 10 / 0 | 10 / 0 |
| 32-gon r5, 64-gon r5, 64-gon r5 bored at 4.99 | 0 / 0 at every diameter |
| 64-gon r13, 128-gon r30 | 6 / 6 at d 1; 0 / 0 at d 2-9 |

Straight plunges through the solid law alone, axis declared at the hole centre:
- Octagon r5, centred tool r 4.60 / 4.63 / 4.65 / 4.70 / 4.90 / 4.99: PR 0 / 1 / 1 / 1 / 1 / 1; main 0 at every radius. The flats are at 4.62, so the PR is right at each radius.
- 64-gon r5 and 23-gon r5 (sag 0.047), tool r 5.000 / 5.005 / 5.01 / 5.02: 0 / 0 / 1 / 1, the same as main. This is the round-wall control: no new false conviction.
- 32-gon r5 at full r 5: a vertical axis or a reversed (-Z) axis is excused (0). A tilted axis (0.1 rad), a NaN position, a zero or infinite direction, or an axis 0.3 mm off the bore each excuse nothing (1). All of these fail closed, with no panic.

### Requested before merge
None.

### Questions / notes (not blocking)
1. **What is still forgiven.** Any facet whose sagitta about any declared axis is at most 0.05 mm may still be entered by up to 0.05 + `allow` (0.06 mm). With several holes on one op, a flat of one hole can read as "round" about a distant second hole's axis (for example a D-flat 3 mm long about an axis 96 mm away). In my D-bore probe the adjacent top-cap facet still convicted it, and the amount is bounded by the same cap the decision record accepts. A later tightening could read each facet only about the nearest declared axis, or require its nearest vertex to lie within a fit tolerance of that hole's radius. The record weighed and dropped the radius test. Worth keeping in mind as a P7 follow-up, not a blocker.
2. **Small tools in large round holes (seen on main as well).** A 1 mm end mill in a 64-gon r13 or a 128-gon r30 gets 6 blocking gouges both on main and here. One possible contributor: when the facet half-chord exceeds the tool radius, the old dip bound returns 0, so no excuse is given. I did not isolate the cause, and this PR does not change it. It may deserve its own issue (a legal program refused, P3 if confirmed).
3. **Coarse holes now convict, as intended.** A 16-gon on r5 (sag 0.096) now convicts at any tool of 2 mm or more. The body and the decision record state this as the safe side. A user with a coarse STL hole will need a finer export.
4. **PR #1099.** It changes the same `SolidIndex::hits` signature and `contain_into`, and calls the removed `chord_dip`, so whichever PR merges second needs a careful keep-both. The two do not yet end with one rule: #1099's `thread_bore.rs` `wall_radius` and `material_source.rs` `major_rims` still measure by vertices. They will only share one rule if #1099 switches to `hole_wall::facet_sag` / `wall_excuse` when it takes main. Please carry that into #1099's review.
5. **File size.** `generate.rs` was already far over 400 lines (3275) and grows to 3284. `contain_into` now needs `#[allow(clippy::too_many_arguments)]`, which a small params struct could replace later.
6. **Not exercised by me:** a full Thread op end to end (main's region law refuses it first, as the body says), a 3+2 posed Drill or Bore, and real STEP or STL parts beyond the suites. STEP meshes are made at a chord of at most 0.005 mm (`import/step.rs` `MAX_CHORD`), well under the 0.05 cap, so STEP holes should not be newly convicted.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.
